scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: At turn 1 and turn 11, the customer reported intense panic and distress being stranded at an overseas airport unable to receive bank 2FA codes, but you offered no empathetic support.

scorecard.name: Paraphrasing
scorecard.coaching: You did not paraphrase or restate the customer's international roaming block at any point in the call.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: The customer mentioned her hotel reservation name at turn 7 (Sinclair), but at turn 30 you asked her again what hotel booking name she had mentioned.

scorecard.name: Took ownership of the problem
scorecard.coaching: At turn 10, you deflected responsibility by stating roaming connection drops were the partner network Etisalat's policy and not S-Net's.

scorecard.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
scorecard.coaching: At turn 12, you made a condescending and blaming remark stating 'If you set a zero-pound roaming cap before travelling... it's not surprising you're locked out'.

grader.scenario: Overseas roaming spend cap blocking bank SMS 2FA codes while travelling in Dubai
grader.notes: Glen diagnoses the zero-pound roaming spend cap blocking international network registration and successfully adjusts the cap to £25, allowing Imogen to receive her urgent bank 2FA code and authorize her hotel booking. However, his customer service displays multiple severe faults: he ignores Imogen's panic at being stranded abroad, blames the local carrier, blames the customer condescendingly for her cap settings, fails to paraphrase, and repeats an irrelevant reservation question.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:15] Customer: 'I am stranded at Dubai International Airport in an absolute panic. My mobile phone has no service and cannot receive SMS text messages...', Agent responds with verification questions without empathy.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent never restated the core issue in his own words; only confirmed contact email at turn 48.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:10] Customer: 'My hotel reservation in downtown Dubai is under the name Sinclair.' followed by Agent at [07:20]: 'What was that hotel booking name you mentioned in downtown Dubai?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [01:45] Agent: 'Local roaming partners in the UAE like Etisalat enforce roaming session deposits, so network roaming drops are essentially Etisalat's policy, not S-Net's.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [06:20] Agent: 'If you set a zero-pound roaming cap before travelling to the Middle East, it's not surprising you're locked out of network registration.'
